Package io.webagent4j.wait

package io.webagent4j.wait
The one deterministic polling/deadline primitive shared by locator resolution, verification polling, and action stabilization - not three independent timers.

WaitEngine.await(io.webagent4j.wait.WaitBudget, io.webagent4j.wait.WaitPolicy, io.webagent4j.wait.IWaitProbe) owns exactly four things: when to poll, when to stop, how much time remains, and when a satisfied result has been stable long enough. It owns nothing about what is being waited for - that is entirely the caller's IWaitProbe, a side-effect-free reading. WaitBudget is a monotonic, saturating deadline that can be shared across sequential sub-operations, each seeing a shrinking remaining() rather than a fresh timeout. IMonotonicClock is never measured against wall-clock time, which can jump on an NTP correction or daylight-saving change.

This package knows nothing about DOM elements, locators, or browser actions; those domains (webagent4j-locator, webagent4j-verification, webagent4j-action) are adapters built on top of it. See docs/wait-and-stability.md for the full per-domain breakdown and the exactly-once backend-execution guarantee this engine never compromises.

    Description
    IMonotonicClock
    Source of monotonic time for deadline arithmetic.
    IWaitProbe<T>
    A single, side-effect-free reading of some external condition.
    IWaitSleeper

    IWaitSleeper.SystemWaitSleeper
    LockSupport-backed sleeper used outside of tests.
    WaitBudget
    A monotonic deadline, optionally shared across several sequential sub-operations.
    WaitEngine
    The one deterministic polling coordinator shared by every domain that needs to wait for a condition: locator resolution, verification, and action stabilization/postconditions.
    WaitInterruptedException
    Signals that a wait was stopped because the current thread was interrupted, either before or during a sleep between polls.
    WaitPolicy
    Immutable polling cadence: how often to probe and, optionally, how long a satisfied result must remain continuously satisfied before it is accepted.
    WaitResult<T>
    Outcome of one WaitEngine.await(WaitBudget, WaitPolicy, IWaitProbe) call.
    WaitSample<T>
    One side-effect-free reading taken by an IWaitProbe.
    WaitSample.Status
    Whether a sample currently satisfies the awaited condition.
    WaitStatus
    Terminal outcome of a WaitEngine.await(WaitBudget, WaitPolicy, IWaitProbe) call.
